concepts.headline: HOLIDAY SALE FOR NURSES
concepts.primary_text: At 6:45 AM when you tie your laces in the locker room, your shoes feel fine. By 2:00 PM on the unit, your heels feel like they are pounding straight into bare concrete. And by 7:15 PM, you are doing that exhausted limp across the hospital parking lot to your car, dreading having to stand up and cook dinner when you get home. Most of us spent $160 on fancy running sneakers because someone said they were comfortable. And because your feet naturally swell by half a size over a long shift, that narrow toe box ends up pinching your toes like a clamp. Sizing up does not work because your heel slips, and adding insoles just eats your toe room. The Ortho Stretch Cushion Shoe was engineered for women who actually stand all day. Here are direct answers to the three questions women ask us most. 1. Does it really have real arch support? Yes. Firm, podiatrist-recommended anatomical arch support is molded right into the base of the shoe. It does not compress into mush after two weeks, and you do not have to buy separate insoles. 2. What if I have wide feet, bunions, or swelling? The entire upper is made from a breathable stretch-knit weave. It shapes itself around your foot and flexes as your feet swell throughout the day, without squeezing your toes into a narrow point. 3. Are the laces a hassle? There are no laces to tie.
